issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi,

I have an external DB that I connect to via the SQL integration but after a while I can see ca. 5000 entries per day with the following message

Can't reconnect until invalid transaction is rolled back. Please rollback() fully before proceeding (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/8s2b)

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.6.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SQL

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

_No response_


I can confirm that I've got the same issue after network reconnects or network outages of a couple of minutes (which happen frequently).
I'm, using Home Assistant 2023.10.3 and MariaDB 10.5.

I'm connecting to this remote mariadb server through an SSH tunnel and when the SSH tunnel is reconnected after a network outage, I see that a SQL query failed, which is to be expected:
```
2023-10-23 00:05:56.461 ERROR (SyncWorker_6) [homeassistant.components.sql.sensor] Error executing query SELECT dailytotal FROM solar ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1: (MySQLdb.OperationalError) (2002, "Can't connect to server on '127.0.0.1' (115)")
(Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/e3q8)
```
But directly after the connection recovers, I get the following error messages, repeated until I restart home assistant:
```
2023-10-23 00:09:56.470 ERROR (SyncWorker_4) [homeassistant.components.sql.sensor] Error executing query SELECT dailytotal FROM solar ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1: Can't reconnect until invalid transaction is rolled back.  Please rollback() fully before proceeding (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/8s2b)

Please rollback() fully before proceeding (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/20/8s2b)
```
I don't need to restart MariaDB - a restart of home assistant is sufficient for the request to work again.
Does a reload of the `sql` integration solve it or only by a full HA restart?

sqlalchemy sessions are thread local so once it goes wrong in one thread its going to block any other transactions in that thread

`recorder.util.session_scope` has a helper for this.
